Value-at-Risk (VaR) vs. Potential Future Exposure (PFE): Twins Across the Market Risk and Counterparty Credit Risk (CCR) domains.

VaR and PFE are often understood as twin metrics because both isolate tail risk using high-confidence statistical quantiles (typically 95% or 99%).

However, applying them on a risk desk requires recognizing their structural and operational differences. See how the two metrics break down across four core dimensions:

🔹 Mathematical Mechanics
Both metrics rely on Monte Carlo or historical simulation to model portfolio MTM distributions and capture correlation dynamics. However, the key difference is they evaluate opposite tails of the MTM value distribution - market risk focuses on losses while CCR focuses on gains.

🔹 Structural Behavior
VaR measures market risk by tracking two-sided portfolio mark-to-market fluctuations. PFE measures counterparty credit risk and enforces a hard floor at zero ((MtM,0)) because negative portfolio values represent your liabilities and not credit exposure to your counterparty - hence irrelevant for CCR purposes.

🔹 Temporal Dynamics
VaR models short-term horizons (1-day to 10-day FRTB SA capital requirements) under a static portfolio assumption. PFE projects dynamic exposure profiles across multi-year time grids (up to 30 years), generally rising early due to diffusion risk of underlying portfolio risk factors before decaying as trades mature.

🔹 Operational Mitigation
VaR / market risk is reduced via position liquidation or delta hedging where market liquidity is an important consideration. CCR / PFE is reduced via Credit Support Annex (CSA) mechanics, including Margin Period of Risk (MPoR), collateral thresholds, and close-out netting benefits.

Source: Ray Yeo
